claims.explanation: Vinorelbine is a tubulin-polymerization inhibitor, so selectivity is most plausibly driven by the cellular context that determines mitotic dependence and drug efflux/handling rather than by a single lineage. The killed lines are enriched for TP53 pathway loss plus co-occurring PI3K/RTK-RAS/MAPK alterations (e.g., PIK3CA, PTEN, KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, MET), which together increase reliance on microtubule-dependent mitosis and reduce apoptotic restraint, while the protected lines are enriched for wild-type TP53 or intact p53 signaling and for efflux/RTK contexts that blunt vinorelbine response. Features such as high TUBB3 or ABCB1 expression and damaging TP53/PIK3CA/PTEN mutations are therefore expected to predict sensitivity, whereas intact p53 and low tubulin/efflux expression predict protection

features.basis: Damaging TP53 mutations are highly enriched in the selectively killed lines and impair mitotic/apoptotic checkpoint responses to microtubule poisons.
Hotspot PIK3CA mutations co-occur in several killed lines (HGC27, 22RV1, HCC1954) and may increase mitotic dependency.
Damaging PTEN loss appears in multiple killed lines (NCIH1339, FTC238, WM793, RL952, HEC265) and may reduce survival signaling restraint.
KRAS mutations are common in killed lung/pancreas lines (NCIH1339, PATU8988T, NCIH1792) and may increase reliance on microtubule dynamics.
BRAF mutations appear in killed melanoma/thyroid/endometrial lines (WM793, 8305C, RL952, HEC265) and may sensitize to mitotic stress.
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (PC14, HCC4006) are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival signaling blunts vinorelbine.
High TUBB3 (beta-III tubulin) expression is a known mediator of resistance to tubulin-polymerization inhibitors.
High ABCB1/MDR1 efflux pump expression reduces intracellular vinorelbine and is a canonical resistance mechanism.
Damaging SMARCA4 mutations appear in several killed lines (NCIH1339, FTC238, NCIH1703) and may impair chromatin-based survival responses.
CDKN2A loss is frequent in killed lines (NCIH1339, NCIH1703, KELLY, 8305C, SCABER) and may increase mitotic dependence.
Damaging ATM mutations appear in killed lines (RL952, 8305C, SNU685) and may impair DNA-damage/mitotic checkpoint responses.
Damaging ARID1A mutations appear in several killed lines (22RV1, RL952, HEC265) and may alter chromatin-dependent drug responses.
